commit_scope: Keep readable Hati presence identities resolvable when their inside Refine doorway reaches the editor through a slug or alias.
evidence_refs: The in-app browser showed that https://hati.earth/people/urs renders normally while its expanded Refine doorway targets /people/urs-muff/edit, which rendered the site's soft-404 view despite returning HTTP 200.

The same browser session rendered /people/contributor%3Aseeker71/edit as the intended editor, proving that the inside page existed and that identity resolution, rather than routing or deployment, was the broken boundary.
The display and edit routes now use one resolver for canonical graph ids, bare contributor ids, human-readable slugs, and declared aliases.
The public deploy verifier now requires the expected rendered profile and editor titles, so an HTTP-200 soft 404 fails the rollout contract.
Browser and command evidence records only route state and public headings; private profile or account content is intentionally excluded.

local_validation.summary: The shared resolver tests, full web suite, production build, strict spec gate, commit-evidence validation, and combined local web/API verifier pass. The local in-memory API intentionally lacks production contributor graph data, so the exact data-backed editor rendering is covered by unit proof and the public deployment gate.

test_flows: Open /people/urs, expand its substrate footprint, and follow Refine.

Request a canonical graph id and verify that no contributor-list scan occurs.
